evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫, Chinese University of Hong Kong
evidence.field: 甲骨文、金文用例及形義源流通解
evidence.text: The database describes oracle-bone and bronze forms as resembling a tool. One proposal identifies a bladed tool whose upper part may have served as a carpenter’s square; other proposals identify a square or a building tool. These are competing interpretations. The entry reports oracle-bone uses as a state or place name, a status or occupation term, and a whole-graph loan for 貢. It cites examples 多工 in Heji 19433, 百工 in Tunnan 2525, 工(貢)冊 in Heji 38310, and 工(貢)父甲三牛 in Heji 27462, but does not date those artifacts in the displayed text.
evidence.title: 漢字甲骨部件分析：工

evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫, Chinese University of Hong Kong
evidence.text: The database reports 工 as an official title in a bronze inscription interpreted as 司空, 工師 in bronze weapon inscriptions, and 工 used for 功 (‘achievement’) in several bronze inscriptions. It also cites a Warring States bamboo-slip use read as 功 in 上博竹書一《孔子詩論》簡5. These attestations support early graphic interchange in specific contexts, but the page does not give artifact dates for each example or establish a semantic chain from a tool to work and achievement.
evidence.title: 漢字甲骨部件分析：工

evidence.source: Shuowen.org, text of 說文解字 and 段玉裁注
evidence.field: 說文解字 工 entry; commentary
evidence.text: The transmitted Shuowen entry says 工 means 巧飾, explains the form as a person possessing 規矩, and compares it with 巫. It records 𢒄 as an ancient form of 工 written with 彡. Duan Yucai associates 巧飾 with skilled finishing. This is a historical lexicographic account, not independent proof of the graph’s original referent or of an ancestor-to-descendant relationship between 𢒄 and 工.
evidence.title: 說文解字「工」

evidence.field: Middle Chinese and Old Chinese pronunciation
evidence.text: The entry gives Guangyun fanqie 古紅切, Middle Chinese Baxter transcription kuwng, Baxter–Sagart Old Chinese *kˤoŋ, and Zhengzhang Old Chinese *koːŋ. These are reconstructions in named systems, not ancient recordings. The same page lists Standard Mandarin gōng and Standard Cantonese gung1. No sound component occurs within 工 itself.
evidence.title: 工 - Wiktionary, the free dictionary

evidence.text: The entry places 工, 功, and 攻 in Zhengzhang’s 工 phonetic series and gives 工 and 功 as *koːŋ, while 攻 is *koːŋ or *kuːŋ. These reconstructions support a close sound correspondence within that system; they do not alone prove that the associated senses descend from one word or establish a semantic sequence.
evidence.title: 工 - Wiktionary, the free dictionary

gaps: The precise object depicted by the early 工 graph remains disputed: the inspected paleographic source records a bladed tool with a possible square function, a square interpretation, and a building-tool interpretation.

The proposed graph-as-tool account does not establish the spoken name or pronunciation of the depicted object. 工’s reconstructed pronunciation cannot independently identify that object’s name; no separate name evidence was found.

The CUHK entry lists artifact identifiers but does not date each one in its displayed text. The earliest dated attestation for the tool graph, place or state name, official/status sense, craft occupation, work, achievement, and 貢 loan remains unverified.
The semantic route from proposed tool image to craft, worker, work, skill, and achievement is not established as one chronology. Shuowen’s 巧飾 explanation differs from the modern tool analysis.

The reported 工(貢) forms are whole-graph loans, separate from any sound-component analysis; no early borrowing pronunciation comparison or independently established 貢 sound evidence was found in the inspected pages.

工 has no internal sound component to classify. Shuowen’s 𢒄 is recorded as an alternate ancient graph with 彡, but the inspected sources do not establish whether it is an ancestor, variant, or other relation to 工.

The official Xiaoxuetang 工 query did not yield inspectable individual candidate labels or image URLs in the browser tool. The CUHK-linked image endpoints likewise lacked inspectable provenance. Thus no image candidate met the identity and reuse-provenance threshold.

limitations.text: No glyph image is proposed. Searches and inspected pages did not establish a specific 工 historical glyph image with verified form identity and image provenance. Xiaoxuetang’s CC0 notice applies to query-interface glyph images, but a specific 工 image was not retrievable; CUHK’s linked image endpoints were not inspectable. Commons results were either general samples or unrelated characters.
